subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Smith <lauren@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap - Hosted vs Dedicated requirements

Hi Lauren - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what I heard and next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of customer requirements (from our call):
- Peak traffic: ~500 requests/sec (spiky, 10-15 minute bursts during payroll cutover).
- Typical request: ~60 tokens input, ~120 tokens generated.
- Latency goals: p50 ~120ms, p95 < 300ms end-to-end for synchronous inference.
- SLO sensitivity: financial workflows must stay under p95 300ms; occasional background jobs can be higher latency.
- Data posture: initially ok with hosted API for dev; production needs preference for isolated capacity and predictable throughput.

Initial recommendation (high level):
- Dedicated capacity is the safer production choice given sustained peak throughput and strong p95 needs - reserved GPU pools avoid noisy neighbors and provide predictable tail latency.
- Hosted API is a good ramp path for integration and early validation (we can do a short pilot) but would need capacity planning and fallback policies for cutover bursts.

Attachments: I attached a short brief comparing Hosted vs Dedicated and a CSV with our recent latency/throughput benchmarks for the model families we discussed.

Open questions / items I promised to follow up on:
1) Can you confirm the concurrency per request (do you fan out single end-user requests or are these 1:1)?
2) What SLA/uptime requirements will procurement expect for production?
3) Do you have any hard limits on egress/data residency?

Suggested next steps:
- If you agree, we can schedule a capacity-sizing call with our infra team (Marissa) to map 500 req/s to a Dedicated config and cost.
- We can also stand up a 2-week hosted trial to validate integration and latency profiles before committing.

If that works I'll loop in Marissa to coordinate capacity sizing and provide a rough cost estimate.

Thanks - Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Lauren Smith <lauren@finpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap - Hosted vs Dedicated requirements

Thanks Neha - that matches our notes. Quick answers to your questions:
- Concurrency: most requests are 1:1 (no heavy fan-out). Concurrent open sessions during peak ~400-500, so requests line up with the peak rate.
- SLA: Procurement will want 99.9% uptime and an understanding of mitigation options for degraded performance windows.
- Data residency: US-only for now; no on-prem requirement today.

We are open to doing a hosted trial first (want to validate integration and end-to-end latency), but we need confidence that production will meet the p95 target. If Dedicated gives a clear path to meeting p95 at 500 req/s with documented tail latency, that will be preferable for the final go-live.

Can we get a short capacity assessment and a cost comparison (hosted pilot vs dedicated reserved) to share with procurement next week?

Cheers,
Lauren
Director of Product - FinPay
lauren@finpay.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency & throughput follow-up

Lauren - perfect, thanks for the clarifications. Below is a concise tradeoff + proposed plan so procurement has something concrete.

Tradeoffs (short):
- Dedicated: Pros = predictable tail latency, reserved throughput, stronger isolation (meets procurement comfort). Cons = commit/contract needed, higher upfront cost but lower unit token $ at scale.
- Hosted: Pros = fastest to start, no upfront commit, simpler procurement. Cons = subject to multi-tenant variability under extreme bursts unless we reserve burst capacity or configure autoscale pools and fallbacks.

Mapping to your numbers:
- For 500 req/s with ~180 tokens total per request (input+output), our rough estimate shows Dedicated configurations (reserved 8-12 GPUs depending on model quantization) will reliably hit p95 < 300ms. We'll produce a sizing matrix on the call.

Proposed plan (recommended):
1) Two-week hosted pilot (quickest path to validate integration + p50 latency). We'll instrument tracing and token-level cost during this trial.
2) Concurrent capacity-sizing session for Dedicated (Marissa leads). If sizing indicates Dedicated is needed for production, we'll present cost/commit options and a migration plan.

Deliverables I'll provide this week:
- Capacity-sizing spreadsheet (how 500 req/s maps to GPU pools) - Marissa will share.
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison (TCO over 6/12 months).
- POC success criteria (latency, error rate, throughput) and suggested canary rollout plan.

Can we schedule the capacity-sizing call on Friday (2000 UTC / 12:00 PT)? If that time doesn't work, suggest 10:00 PT on Monday.

Next steps: looping Marissa for sizing and pricing.

Best,
Neha
